explanation: An employer's usual answer to a strike is replacement labor, and the choice explaining that strikers "kept the machines occupied" so that an employer "could not simply bring in replacement workers" says why that answer failed. The choice reasoning that "most sit-downs lasted less than a week" so an employer had "none at all in which to go to court" credits the tactic's force to its brevity, which the notes never do; the choice counting "583 sit-downs in the two peak years" gives scale; and the choice ending "once the courts ruled the tactic unlawful in 1939" says why the sit-down ended, not why it was hard to fight.
